messages.author: f885e974e72cf61d
messages.subject: Questions on warping meshes & plotting landmarks
parts:
Hi geomorph community,

I'm working on visualization of my brain shape data, and I have questions around the (1) plotReftoTarget function and (2) plotspec. For my project, I'm examining variation in brain shape among mustelid (badger/weasel/otter) species. 

(1) I'm using plotReftoTarget to predict the shapes at the PC extremes. When considering the reference specimen, is it more appropriate to use the mean shape estimated from all the individual specimens or from species averages? There is a notable difference in the result, and surface meshes using the mean shape of all the individuals in the dataset (attachment: PC1...INDMEAN) look more like what I expected given the point and vector plots. I presume this discrepancy is related to the species mean being an average of an [species] average?

Also, I did check the scaling, though I'm unsure how to interpret/correct for this difference. 
> range(gvitatta.ply$vb[1:3]) [1] -1.277344 1047.774780 > range(gvitatta.coords) [1] -54.59414 1064.74500

Tangentially related -- is there a way to move the "light source?" I did not change anything in my code other than the reference specimen, and the lighting has shifted. The plot is well-lit dorsally but not laterally or posteriorly.

(2) Re: plotspec - I have both curve and surface semilandmarks. Is there any way to delineate and plot the curve SLs in a different color alongside the fixed landmarks?

Thank you for your time, and I look forward to your advice and insights.

All the best,
Ani

parts:
Ani,

 

For visualizing deformations it is generally advised to use the overall mean of the dataset as the ‘reference’. So from your question that would mean the mean of the individuals, which is the consensus from the GPA.

 

Re lighting: Not sure on this one: geomorph does nothing regarding lighting of the surfaces.

 

Point colors: One could in theory obtain the output object, recolor manually, and then plot it.

 

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Questions on warping meshes & plotting landmarks
parts: (2) Re: plotspec - I have both curve and surface semilandmarks. Is there any way to delineate and plot the curve SLs in a different color alongside the fixed landmarks?

To answer your question most philosophically, there is always a way to plot what you want in R, as long as you are comfortable with R graphics.  But if you meant is there a way to manipulate geomorph functions without having to write complicated r scripts for graphics, then the answer is, “maybe”.

For example, one could do something like this:

> library(geomorph)
> data("pupfish")
> plotAllSpecimens(pupfish$coords, plot_param = list(pt.bg = c(rep(1, 20), rep(2, 36)), mean.bg = c(rep(1, 20), rep(2, 36))))

You could do something similar making sure to match colors with landmark numbers (the example above was simplistic and sloppy).  The plotAllSpecimens function is useful for quick plotting but maybe not as elegant as “do it yourself” plotting (because it lacks some capability of changing plotting parameters).  If you want the most control over your plots, there simply is no substitute for R graphics skill  For example, this is what I might do instead of above.


> library(geomorph)
> data("pupfish")
> 
> plot(pupfish$coords[,,1],
+      type = "n",
+      asp = 1,
+      xlim = c(-0.25, 0.25),
+      ylim = c(-0.1, 0.1),
+      xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
+      xlab = "", ylab = "",
+      bty = "n")
> 
> for(i in 1:length(pupfish$CS)) {
+   points(pupfish$coords[,, i],
+        pch = 16,
+        col = c(rep(1, 20), rep(2, 36)),
+        cex = c(rep(1, 20), rep(0.5, 36))
+        )
+ }
> points(mshape(pupfish$coords),
+        pch = 16, col = “gray”, cex = 0.6)

The point of this is that you can used canned functions with some capability of manipulating plot parameters or you can take complete control of the plot parameters.  Either way, yes you can change landmark colors based on type of landmark.

Best,
Mike

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Questions on warping meshes & plotting landmarks
parts:
It is harder to control low-level openGL features like lighting and shading in R. If you want to have better visualization of meshes, use a proper 3D rendering program like 3D Slicer that supports many different shading and surface rendering techniques. You can do couple things:
1. You can export your deformed meshes (extremes) as PlYs and render them in 3D Slicer
2 If you want more interactivity, and possibly want to make animations of transformation, you can export your geomorph results to SlicerMorph, and then use the GPA module in SlicerMorph to do the visualizations. We have a function called geomorph2slicermorph2 to do that. There is some documentation of this, but feel free to reach out if it is not clear enough.
https://github.com/SlicerMorph/SlicerMorphR?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-run-a-geomorph-analysis-with-slicermorph-data-and-get-the-results-back-into-slicermorph-for-visualization
